**Doggerland – the southern North Sea**

During the Last Glacial Maximum (roughly 20 000 years ago) sea level was some 120 – 130 m below present levels. The area that now makes up the southern North Sea – commonly known as **Doggerland** – was a low‑lying dryland. It stretched across what is today the English Channel, the North Sea, and parts of the coasts of Britain, France, Belgium, the Netherlands, northern Germany and Jutland.

In short, aside from the Irish Channel and the shallow sea adjacent to the former Atlantic Hotel (which is essentially the old estuarine/foreshore of the Thames/English Channel), **Doggerland** was the major body of water that was dry land during the last ice age.
